# The Anybuild file

An `Anybuild` file describes how a project is built and served. It is real
[Starlark](https://starlark-lang.org/): `anybuild generate` (or the default
`auto` mode) writes one for you by detecting the project type and its typed
provider configuration. From that point on the file is yours — edit it,
extend it, or replace it entirely.

```python
# Generated by Anybuild v0.23.0 — https://anybuild.run
# This file is yours to edit: add steps or override the serve below.

load("//anybuild/tools:python.bzl", "python_build", "python_config", "python_serve")

config = python_config(
    schema = 1,
    commands = {
        "start": "python main.py",
    },
    python_main_file = "main.py",
    python_version = "3.13",
    uv_version = "0.8.15",
)

build = python_build(config)

python_serve(config, build, name = "my-app")
```

Every provider ships config, build, and serve functions in the bundled
standard library:

- `<provider>_config(...)` constructs the typed provider config embedded in
  the generated file and applies environment and JSON overrides.
- `<provider>_build(config, ...)` returns a **build struct**: the build
  steps, the packages the runtime will need because of this build, the
  mounts it filled, and env vars the serve must set.
- `<provider>_serve(config, build, ...)` wires a serve around any build
  struct: start command, runtime deps, env, mounts, services.

The seam between the two is the composition point. A static-site generator
pairs its own build with the shared static serve; Laravel is a PHP build
with a Node asset build folded into its phases; mkdocs is a Python build
feeding a static serve. Your file can do the same.

For projects living in a subdirectory of the workspace, the generated file
carries a marker the CLI reads back:

```python
app_subdir = "apps/dashboard"
```

## Customizing a generated file

Every `<provider>_serve` accepts the same override surface (forwarded to the
generic assembler in `//anybuild:serve.bzl`):

| Parameter        | Effect                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | Deployment name (generated files bake the directory name) |
| `provider`       | Deployment identity label (defaults per provider)       |
| `build_pre`      | Steps to run before the build struct's steps            |
| `build_post`     | Steps to run after the build struct's steps             |
| `extra_env`      | Additional serve-time env vars                          |
| `extra_commands` | Additional command entries                              |
| `commands`       | Base commands dict (`start`, `after_deploy`, ...)       |
| `env`            | Serve-time env vars (merged with the build's)           |
| `prepare`        | Commands run once after the build, before serving       |
| `cwd`            | Working directory of the serve                          |
| `mounts` / `volumes` / `services` | Extra mounts, persistent volumes, services |

```python
load("//anybuild/tools:node.bzl", "node_build", "node_config", "node_serve")

config = node_config(
    schema = 1,
    commands = {"start": "node server.js"},
    node_server = "node",
    node_version = "24",
)

build = node_build(config)

node_serve(
    config,
    build,
    name = "my-app",
    build_post = [run("node scripts/prerender.js", group = "build")],
    extra_env = {"NODE_ENV": "production"},
    services = [service("db", "postgres")],
)
```

Conditional steps are idiomatic: `None` entries in step lists are dropped,
so `run("...") if config.app_subdir else None` works anywhere steps go.

## Builtins

These are available in every Anybuild file and stdlib module:

| Builtin                                    | Meaning                                        |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `dep(name, version = None)`                 | A package (build or runtime dependency)        |
| `use(*deps)`                                | Make packages available to later build steps   |
| `run(cmd, group=, inputs=, outputs=)`       | Run a shell command during the build           |
| `copy(source, target = None, ignore=, base=)` | Copy from the project (or `base = "assets"`) |
| `workdir(path)`                             | Change the build working directory             |
| `env(**vars)`                               | Set env vars for subsequent build steps        |
| `write(path, content)`                      | Write a file during the build                  |
| `path(dir)`                                 | Prepend a directory to `PATH`                  |
| `mount(name)`                               | A named mount: `.path` (build) / `.serve_path` (serve) |
| `volume(name, serve_path)`                  | A persistent volume mounted at serve time      |
| `service(name, provider)`                   | A backing service: `postgres`, `mysql`, `redis` |
| `file_exists(relpath)`                      | Probe the app source tree (see below)          |
| `config(provider, schema, **fields)`         | Low-level typed config constructor used by provider config helpers |
| `PORT`                                      | The configured port, as a string               |

`run()` groups (`install`, `build`, `prune`, ...) tag steps so CLI command
overrides know which step to replace. `$PORT` inside `start`/`after_deploy`
commands is substituted with the configured port.

### `file_exists()`

`file_exists("package.json")` checks the app source tree — the workspace
root, or the app subdirectory for subdir projects. Paths are app-relative;
absolute paths and `..` traversal are rejected. Symlinks are followed, so a
symlinked `wp-content/` counts. Use it for plain existence checks; derived
or overridable values belong in `config`.

## Configuration

The generated file constructs its `config` value with the provider's
`<provider>_config(...)` helper. The arguments are the stable detected
configuration, including pinned runtime versions, so the project definition
is explicit and reproducible. Evaluation applies overrides while constructing
that value. Every field can be overridden without touching the file:

- **Environment variables** with the `ANYBUILD_` prefix:
  `ANYBUILD_PHPIX=true`, `ANYBUILD_NODE_VERSION=22`, `ANYBUILD_WP_VERSION=latest`,
  `ANYBUILD_PYTHON_VERSION=3.12`, `ANYBUILD_STATIC_DIR=dist`, ...
  The legacy `SHIPIT_` prefix remains a fallback when the matching
  `ANYBUILD_` variable is absent.
- **`--config` JSON** merged over the detected values:
  `anybuild build --config '{"phpix": true, "php_version": "8.4"}'`
- **CLI command flags**: `--install-command`, `--build-command`, and
  `--start-command` replace the first step of the matching group (or the
  start command) in the evaluated plan.

Node build commands are inferred from the resolved package manager after
overrides. Generated files omit `node_build_command`; setting it supplies
an explicit command. Regenerate older files to remove a previously inferred
`node_build_command` before switching package managers.

Notable fields per provider (see `crates/anybuild/src/providers/` for the full
sets — common fields `name`, `port`, `services`, `app_subdir`,
`extra_dependencies`, and `autodetected_extra_dependencies` live on the base):

| Provider   | Fields                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| python     | `python_version`, `python_server`, `python_framework`, `asgi_application`, `wsgi_application`, `python_extra_dependencies`, `python_precompile`, `python_extra_index_url` |
| node       | `node_version`, `node_package_manager`, `node_framework`, `node_server`, `node_build_command`, `edgejs_enable`, `edgejs_engine`, `edgejs_precompile`, `optimize_node_dependencies` |
| php        | `php_framework`, `php_version`, `phpix`, `composer_enable`, `composer_build_script`, `php_public_dir` |
| wordpress  | php fields plus `wp_version`, `wp_locale`, `wp_cli_version`    |
| staticfile | `static_dir`, `sws_version`, `static_convert_redirects`               |
| go         | `go_version`, `go_build_file`, `go_serve_binary`                  |

The common `extra_dependencies` field attaches runtime packages to any
provider. Entries accept a package name or `name@version`:

```python
config = node_config(
    schema = 1,
    extra_dependencies = ["sendmail", "ffmpeg"],
    node_version = "24",
)
```

You can also set the field using JSON through an environment variable or
`--config`:

```bash
ANYBUILD_EXTRA_DEPENDENCIES='["sendmail"]' anybuild build --wasmer
anybuild build --wasmer --config '{"extra_dependencies": ["sendmail"]}'
```

Wasmer maps `sendmail` to `sendmail/sendmail@0.1.10`. When the serve
dependencies include `sendmail`, `php`, or `phpix`, the generated `app.yaml`
sets `enable_email: true`. PHP and PHPix already include Sendmail. The
capability depends on runtime packages, so it also applies to Node and Python
apps that attach Sendmail.

The local backend uses the host's Sendmail without installing it; a
Sendmail-compatible command must already be available and configured. Linux
does not guarantee that an MTA is installed. Docker uses Debian's
`sendmail-bin` package, installing it only when `sendmail` is missing, and
keeps its configuration and libraries in the final runtime image. Native
email delivery still requires configuring the MTA for the target environment.

Generated files store detected runtime packages, such as FFmpeg and Pandoc
for Python wrappers, in `autodetected_extra_dependencies`. This list stays
separate from user-supplied `extra_dependencies` through configuration
overrides. Serve assembly merges both lists by package name, with explicit
user versions taking precedence:

```python
autodetected_extra_dependencies = ["pandoc"]
extra_dependencies = ["sendmail", "pandoc@3.6"]
```

An environment or JSON override replaces only the user extras list, so
`ANYBUILD_EXTRA_DEPENDENCIES='["sendmail"]'` preserves the generated Pandoc
dependency even if it is no longer detected from the project files. An empty
user list clears user additions while retaining detected packages. Regenerate
older files to move inferred packages from `extra_dependencies` into
`autodetected_extra_dependencies`.

Use `extra_dependencies` instead of the former serve `extra_deps` argument.
Python packages continue to use `python_extra_dependencies`; Node build tools
use `node_extra_dependencies`.
For packages needed during the build, add `use(dep(...))` in `build_pre`.

For Node apps targeting Wasmer, the optional `edgejs_engine` field accepts
`"quickjs"` or `"external"`. Leaving it unset uses QuickJS by default.
QuickJS uses `wasmer/edgejs-quickjs@0.2.5`, and the external engine uses
`wasmer/edgejs@0.2.5`. Set it in `node_config(...)`, with
`ANYBUILD_EDGEJS_ENGINE=external`, or through a JSON override:
`anybuild build --config '{"edgejs_engine": "external"}'`.

The common `services` field configures typed services. Generated files load
`mysql` or `postgres` from `//anybuild:services.bzl` and render database
services as `services = [mysql()]` or `services = [postgres()]`. Python and
Node runtime providers infer the service from database client dependencies.
Node recognizes `mysql`, `mysql2`, `mariadb`, `@databases/mysql`, `pg`,
`postgres`, `pg-promise`, `slonik`, and `@databases/pg`. Wasmer deployments
use the service to request the matching managed database capability.

## `load()` labels

| Label form                     | Resolves to                                   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `//anybuild/...:file.bzl`     | The bundled standard library                  |
| `//pkg/path:file.bzl`       | `<project root>/pkg/path/file.bzl`         |
| `file.bzl` / `./file.bzl`| Relative to the loading file                  |

So a project can keep its own helpers in `deploy/custom.bzl` and load
them with `load("//deploy:custom.bzl", "my_helper")`.

## Provider reference

| Provider    | Module                              | Config / Build / Serve |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| python      | `//anybuild/tools:python.bzl`       | `python_config` / `python_build` / `python_serve` |
| node        | `//anybuild/tools:node.bzl`         | `node_config` / `node_build` / `node_serve` |
| go          | `//anybuild/tools:go.bzl`           | `go_config` / `go_build` / `go_serve` |
| php         | `//anybuild/tools:php.bzl`          | `php_config` / `php_build` / `php_serve` |
| laravel     | `//anybuild/tools:laravel.bzl`      | `laravel_config` / `laravel_build` / `laravel_serve` |
| wordpress   | `//anybuild/tools:wordpress.bzl`    | `wordpress_config` / `wordpress_build` / `wordpress_serve` |
| staticfile  | `//anybuild/tools:staticfile.bzl`   | `staticfile_config` / `staticfile_build` / `staticfile_serve` |
| hugo        | `//anybuild/tools:hugo.bzl`         | `hugo_config` / `hugo_build` / `staticfile_serve` |
| jekyll      | `//anybuild/tools:jekyll.bzl`       | `jekyll_config` / `jekyll_build` / `staticfile_serve` |
| mkdocs      | `//anybuild/tools:mkdocs.bzl`       | `mkdocs_config` / `mkdocs_build` / `staticfile_serve` |
| node-static | `//anybuild/tools:node_static.bzl`  | `nodestatic_config` / `nodestatic_build` / `staticfile_serve` |

The static family shares one serve: their generated files pass the identity
explicitly — `staticfile_serve(config, build, provider = "hugo")` — because
the `provider` label is deployment identity and belongs to the serve, not
the build.

Providers with flavors take keyword options on the build. The most useful:
`python_build(config, serving = False)` and Node's granular fragments
(`node_toolchain`, `node_install_steps`, `node_build_step`, ...) give you
embeddable builds for composing.

## Composing your own

The stdlib composes the same way user files do. This is a docs site built
by a Python tool and served as static files — essentially what
`mkdocs.bzl` does internally:

```python
load("//anybuild:serve.bzl", "build")
load("//anybuild/tools:python.bzl", "python_build", "python_config")
load("//anybuild/tools:staticfile.bzl", "staticfile_serve")

config = python_config(
    schema = 1,
    python_version = "3.13",
    uv_version = "0.8.15",
)

py = python_build(config, serving = False)
site = mount("static_app")

docs = build(
    steps = py.steps + [
        run("uv run mkdocs build --site-dir={}".format(site.path), group = "build"),
    ],
    serve_deps = py.serve_deps,
    mounts = [site],
    static_app = site,
    static_config = None,
)

staticfile_serve(config, docs, name = "docs", provider = "mkdocs")
```

`build()` (from `//anybuild:serve.bzl`) creates a build struct from steps
plus the convention fields (`serve_deps`, `mounts`, `env`) and any extra
fields downstream serves want — here the `static_app` mount that
`staticfile_serve` reads. `serve()` from the same module is the generic
assembler behind every `<provider>_serve`, with the override surface
documented above.

### Typecho

Typecho source distributions are detected as PHP projects with `php_framework =
"typecho"`. Wasmer uses PHPix by default. The generated serve explicitly mounts
the `typecho-usr` volume at `/app/usr`, preserving configuration, SQLite
databases, uploads, themes, and plugins.

Like WordPress, `after_deploy` seeds the volume with bundled files without
replacing existing content. PHPix creates the `/app/config.inc.php` symlink to
`usr/config.inc.php` at runtime through a dedicated `start-typecho.php` startup
script. The standard `typecho-config.inc.php` template contains only application
and database configuration. Plain PHP loads the persistent config through a
small root loader. Typecho's sources remain unchanged.

Wasmer defaults to `Pdo_Mysql` and requests a managed MySQL database in
`app.yaml`. The template reads Wasmer's `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`,
`DB_PASSWORD`, and `DB_NAME` variables; `TYPECHO_DB_*` variables override them.
Local runs default to SQLite in `usr/typecho.db`. Set
`TYPECHO_DB_ADAPTER=Pdo_SQLite` before building to use SQLite on Wasmer without
requesting a managed database.

The web installer creates the tables and site administrator. An existing
`config.inc.php` is preserved in the volume and loaded as supplied. Custom
configuration must set `__TYPECHO_ROOT_DIR__` to the application root, for
example with `getenv('TYPECHO_APP_PATH')`, because PHP resolves `__FILE__`
through symlinks.

Wasmer runs `after_deploy` as a post-deployment job. For local setup, run
`anybuild run --after-deploy --start` before opening the web installer at
`/install.php`, or use `anybuild run --command=install` with Typecho's
`TYPECHO_DB_*`, `TYPECHO_SITE_URL`, and `TYPECHO_USER_*` environment variables.
The `install` command also seeds the volume before running the installer.

For SQLite on Wasmer, set `TYPECHO_DB_ADAPTER=Pdo_SQLite` and optionally
`TYPECHO_DB_FILE=/app/usr/typecho.db`. Locally, the persistent data lives under
`.anybuild/volumes/typecho-usr`; Wasmer deployments declare the same volume in
`app.yaml`.
